tagline.en: Write sentences that are clear and correct

subtitle.en: Every card has a short rule and 3 questions: capital letters, full stops, commas, apostrophes, and how to build a complete sentence.
subtitle.bn: প্রতিটি কার্ডে ছোট্ট নিয়ম আর ৩টি প্রশ্ন: বড় হাতের অক্ষর, দাঁড়ি, কমা, apostrophe, আর পূর্ণ বাক্য গঠন।

title.bn: বড় হাতের অক্ষর ও শেষ চিহ্ন

hint.en: How a sentence starts and ends
hint.bn: বাক্য কীভাবে শুরু আর শেষ হয়

hint.en: The small marks inside a sentence
Put the words in the right order

rule.en: Use a capital letter to start a sentence, for the word “I”, and for names of people, places, days, months and languages.
rule.bn: বাক্যের শুরুতে, “I” শব্দে, আর মানুষ, স্থান, দিন, মাস ও ভাষার নামে বড় হাতের অক্ষর লাগে।

recap.example: On Monday, Sara and I went to Dhaka.

options.text: my friend Sara lives in Dhaka.
options.why: A sentence must start with a capital letter: My.

options.text: My friend sara lives in dhaka.
options.why: Names of people and places need capitals: Sara, Dhaka.

options.text: My Friend Sara Lives In Dhaka.
options.why: Ordinary words like “friend” and “lives” don’t need capitals.

options.text: My friend Sara lives in Dhaka.

questions.explanation: Capitals for the first word and for names (Sara, Dhaka).

options.text: On monday, I visited my aunt.
options.why: Days of the week need a capital: Monday.

options.text: On Monday, I visited my aunt.
On Monday, i visited my aunt.
options.why: “I” is always a capital letter.

options.text: on Monday, I visited my aunt.
options.why: The first word of a sentence needs a capital: On.

questions.explanation: Capitals for the first word, the day (Monday) and “I”.

questions.prompt: Which word always needs a capital letter?

options.why: “School” is an ordinary word, unless it is part of a name.
“River” only needs a capital in a name, like “the Padma River”.
“Morning” is an ordinary word.

questions.explanation: Names of languages always start with a capital: English, Bangla.

title.en: Full Stop, Question Mark, Exclamation Mark

rule.en: End a statement with a full stop (.), a question with a question mark (?), and a strong feeling with an exclamation mark (!).
rule.bn: সাধারণ বাক্যের শেষে দাঁড়ি (.), প্রশ্নের শেষে প্রশ্নবোধক (?), আর তীব্র অনুভূতির শেষে বিস্ময়সূচক চিহ্ন (!)।

recap.example: I like rice. · Do you like rice? · I love it!

options.why: This sentence asks a question, so it needs ?.
“!” shows strong feeling. This is a question.
A comma can’t end a sentence.

questions.explanation: It asks something, so it ends with a question mark.

options.why: It starts with “What”, but it isn’t asking anything. It shows feeling.
A comma can’t end a sentence.
A semicolon can’t end a sentence.

questions.explanation: “What a …!” shows a strong feeling, so it ends with !.

options.why: It doesn’t ask anything, so no question mark.
A comma can’t end a sentence.
An apostrophe is used inside words, not at the end of a sentence.

questions.explanation: It simply tells us something, so it ends with a full stop.

rule.en: Put commas between items in a list. Before the last item, “and” usually takes the place of the comma.
rule.bn: তালিকার জিনিসগুলোর মাঝে কমা দাও। শেষ জিনিসের আগে সাধারণত কমার বদলে “and” বসে।

recap.example: I like red, blue and green.

options.text: I bought eggs bread and milk.
options.why: You need a comma between “eggs” and “bread”.

options.text: I bought eggs, bread and milk.
I bought, eggs, bread, and, milk.
options.why: Don’t put commas after “bought” or after “and”.

options.text: I bought eggs, bread, milk, and.
options.why: The list can’t end with “and”.

questions.explanation: Commas separate the items, and “and” comes before the last one.

options.why: With only two items, don’t use a comma.
With two items, join them with “and”.
Don’t put a comma after “and”.

questions.explanation: With only two items, use “and” and no comma.

options.text: We need, pens pencils and paper.
options.why: Don’t put a comma after “need”. Put it between the items.

options.text: We need pens pencils, and paper.
options.why: You need a comma between “pens” and “pencils”.

options.text: We need pens, pencils and paper.
We need pens pencils and, paper.
options.why: Don’t put a comma after “and”.

questions.explanation: A comma after “pens”, then “and” before the last item.

title.en: Joining Ideas with And, But, So
title.bn: And, But, So দিয়ে বাক্য জোড়া

cards.badge: idea, but idea · idea, so idea

rule.en: To join two full sentences with and, but or so, put a comma before the joining word. “But” shows a contrast; “so” shows a result.
rule.bn: দুটি পূর্ণ বাক্য and, but বা so দিয়ে জুড়তে সংযোজক শব্দের আগে কমা দাও। “but” বিপরীত বোঝায়, “so” ফলাফল।

recap.example: It was raining, so we stayed inside.

options.text: It was raining, so we stayed inside.
It was raining so, we stayed inside.
options.why: The comma goes before “so”, not after it.

options.text: It was raining, we stayed inside.
options.why: A comma alone can’t join two sentences. Add “so”.

options.text: It was raining. so we stayed inside.
options.why: A new sentence must start with a capital letter.

questions.explanation: Comma before “so”, which joins two full sentences.

questions.prompt: I wanted to play___ I had homework.

options.why: “So” shows a result. Here the ideas are opposite: but.
The comma goes before “but”, not after it.
A new sentence must start with a capital letter.

questions.explanation: The two ideas are opposite, so use “, but”.

questions.prompt: Which word joins two ideas that are opposite?

options.why: “So” shows a result, not a contrast.
“And” adds something similar.
“Because” gives a reason.

questions.explanation: “But” shows a contrast: I’m tired, but I’m happy.

rule.en: An apostrophe shows who owns something (Ali’s bag), or where letters are missing (don’t = do not). For more than one owner ending in -s, put it after the s (the boys’ toys).
rule.bn: Apostrophe দিয়ে মালিকানা (Ali’s bag) বা বাদ পড়া অক্ষর (don’t = do not) বোঝায়। -s-এ শেষ হওয়া বহুবচনে s-এর পরে বসে (the boys’ toys)।

recap.example: Rina’s pen · we’re = we are · the girls’ room

options.why: To show the bag is Ali’s, add an apostrophe: Ali’s.
The apostrophe goes after the name and before the s: Ali’s.
That is a comma. You need an apostrophe: Ali’s.

questions.explanation: The bag belongs to Ali: Ali’s.

options.why: You need an apostrophe where the letter is missing: don’t.
The apostrophe goes where the o is missing: don’t.
That is a comma. You need an apostrophe: don’t.

questions.explanation: do not → don’t. The apostrophe takes the place of the missing o.

questions.prompt: The ___ toys are on the floor. (many boys)

options.why: “Boy’s” means one boy. Here there are many boys.
To show the toys belong to them, you need an apostrophe: boys’.
Plural words ending in s just add the apostrophe: boys’.

questions.explanation: Many boys own the toys: the apostrophe goes after the s.

cards.badge: it’s = it is · its = belongs to it

rule.en: “It’s” is short for “it is” or “it has”. “Its” shows that something belongs to it, and has no apostrophe.
rule.bn: “It’s” মানে “it is” বা “it has”। “Its” মানে তার (মালিকানা), এতে apostrophe নেই।

recap.example: It’s cold. · The dog wagged its tail.

options.why: “Its” means belonging to it. Here we mean “it is”.
There is no word “its’”.
That is a comma. You need an apostrophe.

questions.explanation: It is raining → It’s raining.

options.why: “It’s” means “it is”. “The dog wagged it is tail” makes no sense.
There is no word “its’”.
The tail belongs to the dog, so use its.

questions.explanation: The tail belongs to the dog: its (no apostrophe).

options.why: “Its” shows belonging. Here we mean “it has”.
There is no word “its’”.
That is a comma. You need an apostrophe.

questions.explanation: It has been → It’s been.

rule.en: An English sentence usually goes: subject (who) + verb (does) + object (what). Place and time often come at the end.
rule.bn: ইংরেজি বাক্যের সাধারণ ক্রম: subject (কে) + verb (করে) + object (কী)। স্থান ও সময় সাধারণত শেষে।

recap.example: Rina reads a book in the library every day.

options.why: The subject comes before the verb.
In normal English, the object comes after the verb.
In English, the verb comes before the object (unlike Bangla).

questions.explanation: Subject (Rina) + verb (reads) + object (a book).

questions.prompt: Which sentence has the right word order?

options.text: We played in the park football yesterday.
options.why: The object (football) goes right after the verb.

options.text: Yesterday football we played in the park.
options.why: The object must come after the verb.

options.text: We football played in the park yesterday.
options.why: The verb (played) comes before the object (football).

options.text: We played football in the park yesterday.

questions.explanation: Subject + verb + object, then place, then time.

questions.prompt: What is the subject in “The tall boy kicked the ball”?

options.why: “Kicked” is the verb (the action).
“The ball” is the object (what was kicked).
“Tall” describes the boy. The whole subject is “the tall boy”.

questions.explanation: The subject is who does the action: the tall boy.

rule.en: A complete sentence has a subject and a verb and makes sense on its own. Don’t leave out the verb, and don’t run two sentences together without a full stop or a joining word.
rule.bn: পূর্ণ বাক্যে subject আর verb দুটোই থাকে, আর বাক্যটি একা অর্থ বহন করে। দুটি বাক্য দাঁড়ি বা সংযোজক ছাড়া জুড়ে দিয়ো না।

recap.example: The baby is sleeping. · I was hungry, so I ate.

options.why: The verb is not complete. It needs “is”: is sleeping.
This has no verb and doesn’t make sense alone.
This has no subject. Who is sleeping?

questions.explanation: It has a subject (the baby) and a full verb (is sleeping).

questions.prompt: Which is a run-on sentence (two sentences joined wrongly)?

options.text: I was hungry, so I ate a mango.
options.why: This is correct: a comma and “so” join the two ideas.

options.text: I was hungry. I ate a mango.
options.why: This is correct: two sentences with a full stop.

options.text: Because I was hungry, I ate a mango.
options.why: This is correct: one sentence with a reason.

options.text: I was hungry I ate a mango.

questions.explanation: Two sentences are pushed together with nothing between them.

options.why: “We” has no verb. What did we do?
“Home” is not a full idea. It needs a subject and a verb.

options.text: When the bell rang, we went home.

options.why: The word order is wrong, and it is still not a complete idea.

questions.explanation: Adding the main idea (we went home) makes a complete sentence.
